title.description: A bill's short title where it has one, else its full title; a nomination's nominee, or the post for a military nomination that names nobody

policyArea.description: A bill's CRS policy area (its topic), so a feed can say a vote is in a topic you follow; null for a nomination and for a bill CRS has not classified

MeasureSummary.description: null for a procedural vote that refers to no measure

Position.description: candidate is only used on Speaker elections

choice.description: Candidate named in a Speaker election

partyTotals.description: Per-party counts. An election reports its party split in candidateTotals instead.

candidateTotals.description: Which candidate each party voted for. Only populated when kind = election.

positions.description: How the members named in ?members= voted. Empty when the query names none.

allOf.description: What was voted on, or null for a procedural vote that refers to no measure

votes.description: Yea/nay votes counted: those where the member voted yea or nay and their party was not itself tied

kind.description: From FEC's committee type for another candidate's own committee ('Candidate committee'), else its organization type or leadership-PAC designation; null when FEC classifies the committee as nothing

orgType.description: Raw FEC ORG_TP, so a client can classify differently

cycle.description: The election this campaign is for

receipts.description: Total raised this campaign to date, as the campaign reported it

other.description: Transfers, the candidate's own money, refunds and other receipts

committeesCycle.description: The two-year FEC cycle `committees` covers, which is NOT `cycle`: a senator's campaign may be for 2028 while the committee filings are the 2026 cycle. Null when we hold no committee rows for them.

committees.description: Biggest PAC givers by direct amount. Party and joint fundraising committees are excluded — neither is a PAC check (lesson 23)

MemberFunding.description: funding is null for a member FEC has no current-campaign totals for

choice.description: Candidate named in a Speaker election

allOf.description: null for a procedural vote that refers to no measure, e.g. a motion to adjourn

BillStage.description: Where it stands on the road to law, as BillListItem.stage; null until the worker has staged it

label.description: The plain short label a bill list gives it (BillListItem.label), so a bill followed from its own screen reads as it does in search

summary.description: Latest Congressional Research Service summary, plain text

paragraphs.description: The summary as analysed; citations index into this

stale.description: The bill's summary has changed since; a new analysis is pending. Citations still resolve against paragraphs.

quote.example: extends several expiring programs and authorities

section.description: The bill section, as CRS labels the paragraph; null when it names none

ai.description: Always true: this line was written by AI

allOf.description: null when no purpose line survived verification

part.description: 0 unless the Senate split the nomination into parts

citation.description: As the Senate cites it on the roll call

nomineeName.description: null for military nominations, which promote officers in bulk; show the position instead

positionTitle.example: United States District Judge for the Southern District of Ohio

description.description: Congress.gov's full sentence, including the "vice ..." clause

inSession.description: Sitting now, or within 15 minutes of convening

convenesAt.description: Next (or current) convening, when the chamber has published it

checkedAt.description: When the live worker last polled this chamber

openedAt.description: The floor's own time for the vote (House only)

announcedAt.description: When the worker first saw a floor source name it

postedAt.description: When the worker first saw the roll call XML, polling live; null if it was backfilled

chambers.description: Empty until the live worker has run

votes.description: Open votes named in the last 24 hours, then votes that went final within `since`; newest first

lastNewDataAt.description: When a successful run last stored anything. A scheduled job keeps lastSuccessAt fresh even when upstream stops publishing or nothing is found, so a long gap here, not `stale`, is what shows that

lastError.description: The error of the latest run with an outcome, if it failed; null once a later run succeeds. A run that never recorded an outcome within an hour reads as "abandoned run"

bills.description: Bills in this topic in the Congress

label.description: A plain short label: the short title, or a deterministic rewrite of a long CRS title. The full title is `title`.
label.example: Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act of 2025

allOf.description: Where the measure stands on the road to law; null until the worker has staged it. adopted = a resolution agreed to by every chamber it needs (it never goes to the President); failed = a chamber voted it down (Congress.gov's own marker); vetoed = vetoed and not overridden.

stalled.description: Not settled (law, adopted, vetoed, failed) and no action in 90 days

hasFloorVote.description: At least one recorded roll call on it

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last

billNumber.description: The query read as a bill number ("hr 1013"), so `bills` holds exact matches only

get.summary: Search sitting members by name, state or seat
get.description: `q` is a name (`Schumer`, `alexandria ocasio`), a state by name or code (`New York`, `NY`), or a House seat (`NY-8`, `WY-AL`, `DC-AL`). Sitting members only, delegates and Puerto Rico's resident commissioner included. Senate before House; a name search puts surnames that start with it first. Rate limited per caller.

allOf.description: Only this chamber; omit for both

get.summary: The most recent final votes, newest first

allOf.description: Only this chamber; omit for both

schema.description: Only votes that happened before this: pass the last vote's occurredAt for the next page

Only votes on bills in these topics (CRS policy areas, any case). Repeat it for several, since topic names hold commas. A name that is not one of the topics matches nothing. The Finals tab's Following feed.

200.description: Final votes, newest first (public, max-age=30, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=60)

get.summary: Get a vote with its totals, party breakdown and named members' positions

schema.description: Return these members' own positions on the vote — your delegation, for the vote screen.

get.summary: A member and how often they vote with their own party
Who funds a member's current campaign
get.description: Totals the campaign reported receiving, and the committees that reported giving to it. The two come from different FEC sources and will not reconcile. No individual donor is named: FEC publishes them, Floor does not store them.

schema.description: How many giving committees to return

200.description: The member and their campaign's money

get.summary: Find your district and members of Congress from an address or your location
get.description: Send either `address`, or `lat` and `lng` (for example from the browser's location). Coordinates are rounded to 4 decimal places (about 11 m). Either is sent to the U.S. Census geocoder and is not stored or logged.

400.description: Neither or both of an address and coordinates, or values out of range

404.description: Place not in a U.S. congressional district

get.summary: A member's most recent votes and how they voted
A bill with its summary, sponsor, recent actions and every vote on it
AI analysis of a bill's CRS summary: purpose, provisions, affected groups and impact, each line cited
get.description: Every line is AI-written (`ai: true`) and cites the summary paragraph it came from, quoted verbatim. Lines whose citation didn't check out, or that a second AI pass found unsupported, have been removed. Show `disclaimer` with it.

404.description: No analysis for that bill yet

get.summary: A presidential nomination with every Senate vote on it
What is happening on the floor: each chamber's session state and the votes open or just final

schema.description: Include votes that went final within this many minutes

200.description: Cached at the edge for 5 seconds (public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5, stale-while-revalidate=5)

get.summary: Data freshness for each ingest source

200.description: ok is false when any source is stale

get.summary: The CRS policy areas, with how many bills each holds in a Congress
get.description: All 32 areas, in a fixed order, including ones with no bills yet.

schema.description: Defaults to the Congress in session

get.summary: A topic's bills, newest action first, with where each stands
get.description: filter: all; moving (not settled, acted on in the last 90 days); law; stalled (not settled, no action in 90 days). Settled = law, adopted, vetoed or failed. A bill not yet fetched in detail has stage null and counts as unsettled. Companion bills (the House and Senate versions of one measure) are separate rows and are not linked to each other.

schema.description: Defaults to the Congress in session

400.description: A cursor this route did not issue

404.description: Not one of the policy areas

get.summary: Members, bills and topics in one search
get.description: A bill number in any spelling ("hr 1013", "H.R.1013", "s.j.res.197") returns that bill and nothing else. Otherwise words match bill short titles, titles and CRS summaries (Postgres full-text), topic names, and sitting members exactly as `/v1/members?q=` reads them (the same reader, up to 60, Senate first): a name with accents, hyphens and apostrophes folded ("velazquez", "ocasio cortez"), a state by name or code ("Texas", "N.Y."), or a seat ("TX-35", "DC-1"). `chamber` narrows the members only. Companion bills (the House and Senate versions of one measure) are separate results and are not linked to each other.

allOf.description: Only this chamber; omit for both
